scope:
PHASE 1: Web MVP (master PLAN.md section 14 'Phase 1'; features T1-T7, S1-S5 from section 3; data model section 7; UI spec section 9; sync section 12). No login: the app opens straight to the timeline.
Deliverables:
1. First app open: if there is no settings row, create it with the browser timezone and seed the 'Rise and Shine' and 'Wind Down' tasks (simple one-off tasks for today until recurrence lands in Phase 3, or seed them as recurring rows if the design includes basic recurrence expansion). Idempotent across devices.
2. Data layer: repo functions (tasks, settings) + TanStack Query hooks (useDay, useInbox, useSettings) with optimistic mutations and rollback, client-generated UUIDs, and Supabase Realtime subscriptions that invalidate the right query keys.
3. Day timeline (T4, T5): TaskPill component per PLAN.md section 9.2 (compact timeline, pill height by duration, icon, color, time range, check circle), all-day row, current-time line, completion toggle with animation (T3).
4. Week strip navigation with swipe/keyboard, 'Today' button (T6).
5. Task editor (bottom sheet on mobile, dialog on desktop): title, date/inbox, start time, all-day, duration chips, color swatches (PLAN.md section 8 palette), icon picker (lucide + emoji), subtasks (jsonb), notes, delete (T1, T2).
6. Inbox list with quick add and a 'schedule' action (T7).
7. Responsive shell: mobile bottom tabs + FAB; desktop sidebar + timeline + inbox panel (S5). Light/dark/system theme (S3). Basic settings page (timezone, 12/24h, week start, day start/end, default duration).
8. Tests: Vitest for data mapping and any new core logic; Playwright e2e against a local preview for create / edit / complete / delete / inbox flows; a two-browser-context test proving realtime sync (edit in one, appears in the other within 2 s).
9. Accessibility basics: keyboard navigation, focus management in sheets/dialogs, labels on icon buttons, color contrast in both themes.
Done when: on desktop and a phone browser you can plan today, check tasks off and use the inbox, and an edit on one device appears on the other within about 1 s; all checks green in CI; production deploy works after the release merge.
